thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT DETECTED: KV cache OOM on hosted runtime (model: redwood-open-cc-13b). Pager triggered for oncall-ml. incident_id=INC-20260315-42
marie: saw the page, jumping in. initial symptom: sudden spike in memory on serve-03 causing OOM kill. Users: some 500ms->5s tail lat spikes reported.
josh: seeing a cluster of requests with very long user prompts (~120k tokens). logs show KV cache growth per-request not bounded. stack trace excerpt:```
E 03:14:22 model_inference.cpp:kv_cache_append: failed to allocate 16777216 bytes
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```
sophia: known risk: continuous batching+prefetch was recently rolled to hosted (small %). suspect bad interaction: prefetching full KV for each request without prompt clipping + batching window expansion.
oncall-ml: confirming correlation. metric: kv_cache_bytes_total on serve-03 jumped from 8GB -> 42GB in <2min. continuous_batch_window config shows 2.5s -> 7s at time of surge.
marie: probable cause hypothesis: long prompts cause per-request KV size huge; prefetch tries to pull entire cache for every candidate, continuous batching keeps caches pinned; combined -> runaway memory.
josh: mitigation options: 1) throttle prefetch/prefetch_limit on hosted runtime via config API, 2) disable continuous batching for the hot model, 3) patch runtime to clip KV fetch for >N tokens (longer fix). Need fast mitigation.
oncall-ml: I'm going to disable prefetch for redwood-open-cc-13b on serve-03 and reduce batch window to 1s for all hosted pools as a short-term. Executing.
incident-bot: ACTION STARTED: patching hosted runtime route config. patch_id=patch-187123-a
oncall-ml: runbook command:```bash
# reduce continuous batching window
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/runtime/pools/hosted/actions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"action":"set_batch_window","value_ms":1000}'
```
marie: applying a targeted prefetch throttle on the model route: set `prefetch_limit=4` and `max_prefetch_bytes=10MB` for redwood-open-cc-13b. Patch submitted. jira: RINF-5234.
josh: rolling rollback plan if things break: revert to previous pool config, or toggle routing to fallback model redwood-open-cc-13b-quant (lower mem) for hosted.
incident-bot: UPDATE: prefetch disabled for served route redwood-open-cc-13b on serve-03 by oncall-ml at 03:18:45. memory trend stabilizing.
customer-success: preliminary impact: we saw ~12 customer requests timeout in last 10 minutes; two enterprise customers reported degraded throughput for inference-heavy endpoints. CS will open tickets for affected accounts.
sophia: quick note — logs show one noisy tenant sending concatenated transcripts (customer app bug) that generated the 120k token prompts. Might be a downstream issue we can mitigate via rate limits on token length.
oncall-ml: memory graphs: serve-03 mem usage reduced from 42GB -> 9GB in 3 minutes after prefetch disable and batch window change. CPU and latencies returned to baseline.
marie: pushing hotfix to control-plane: enforce `max_prefetch_bytes=20MB` across hosted pool as guardrail. Doing config push now.
devex-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for control-plane config update. CI shows config diff: -prefetch_limit: 0 -> +prefetch_limit: 4; +max_prefetch_bytes: 20MB.
josh: patched route-level fallback policy: if kv_cache_bytes > 16GB then route to redwood-open-cc-13b-quant. This should reduce future OOM blast radius.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (prefetch throttle, batch window reduced, route fallback). Status: partial mitigation. incident severity -> P1 -> P2.
customer-success: escalation notes: reaching out to the two affected enterprise customers, offering root-cause summary and workaround. Monitoring will continue for 2 hours.
sophia: postmortem items I'm capturing: 1) Add guardrails for prefetching (max bytes, max_items) 2) Add cluster-level circuit breaker for continuous batching when average kv_cache growth rate > X GB/min 3) Add token-length rate limits + customer alerts for extreme prompts 4) Improve dashboarding: per-tenant kv_cache footprint and long-prompt alerts.
oncall-ml: short-term followups assigned: create hotfix PR to default `prefetch_limit=4` for all hosted models (owner=josh), implement route-level circuit-breaker (owner=marie), add alert on kv_cache_growth_rate (owner=oncall-ml).
josh: quick sanity: can we craft a temporary server-side clipping layer that truncates prompt tokens > 50k with a warning header? That avoids customers hitting OOM while we ship fixes.
marie: approved for hosted; please implement with explicit header `X-Prompt-Truncated: true` so SDKs can show in-app message.
incident-bot: HANDOFF: oncall-ml -> oncall-ml-2 (night shift) at 04:00. summary: mitigations applied, memory stabilized, watch kv_cache_bytes_total and long_prompt_count. open actions: implement guardrail PRs, contact affected customers, prepare postmortem.
oncall-ml: handoff checklist posted to /incident/inc-1871234567: includes dashboards, commands to revert patches, and contact list for CS.
customer-success: will post an incident status to affected customers in <30m. will attach temporary mitigation steps for integrators (truncate prompts).
sophia: tagging for postmortem: RINF-5234 root cause likely interaction between continuous batching and aggressive prefetch on extremely long prompts. severity reduced but still need engineering follow-up.
josh: thanks all — good quick coordination. I'll own the hotfix PRs and update this thread with PR links. :thumbsup:
marie: thanks everyone. logging this as P2 and scheduling postmortem doc for tomorrow sync.
devex-bot: Reminder: please include any CLI commands, puppet/terraform diffs, and exact timestamps in the postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated -> monitoring). incident_id=INC-20260315-42. Close reason: prefetch throttled + batch window reduced; no further OOMs.
marie: adding final handoff note: next oncall please ensure we don't re-enable prefetching rollout without canary-specific max_prefetch_bytes and token-length checks.
